docs.title: clusterscope
docs.text:
Technology-agnostic GitOps cluster visualizer CLI + server.

clusterscope parses your GitOps YAML files (Flux or ArgoCD) and generates interactive HTML dashboards showing the dependency graph, sources, kustomizations, and applications of your Kubernetes clusters — with no cluster access required.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Flux & ArgoCD support — auto-detects technology from YAML content
  • Interactive D3.js graph — dependency visualization with hover and click
  • Multi-cluster dashboard — index page linking all cluster profiles
  • Serve mode — live HTTP server with file watcher and auto-reload
  • Live mode — real-time reconciliation status via kubectl
  • PDF export — print-optimized CSS layout via browser print dialog
  • KCL deployment — Kubernetes manifests with git-sync sidecar
  • Backstage integration — catalog-info.yaml for discovery

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
# Single cluster (Flux)
clusterscope -dir ./clusters/prod -out profile.html

# Single cluster (ArgoCD)
clusterscope -dir ./argocd/prod -tech argocd -out profile.html

# Multi-cluster static dashboard
clusterscope -root ./clusters -out ./dist

# Live HTTP dashboard
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters

# Live mode with kubectl enrichment
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters -live -kubeconfig ~/.kube/prod

docs.title: Supported Technologies
docs.text: Technology Parser Resources Flux pkg/flux GitRepository, Kustomization, FluxInstance ArgoCD pkg/argocd Application, ApplicationSet, AppProject

docs.title: Task shortcuts
docs.text:
task ui-serve ROOT=./clusters PORT=8080
task ui-static ROOT=./clusters OUT=./dist
task ui-serve-live ROOT=./clusters KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/prod

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[YAML files on disk] --> B[pkg/flux.ParseDir]
    A --> C[pkg/argocd.ParseDir]
    B --> D[graph.ClusterProfile]
    C --> D
    D --> E[render.WriteHTML]
    D --> F[render.WriteIndex]
    E --> G[cluster.html]
    F --> H[index.html]

    I[kubectl] --> J[internal/live.Enrich]
    J --> D

    K[internal/scan.Root] --> L[multi-cluster mode]
    K --> M[internal/serve.Server]
    M --> N[HTTP /clusters/name]
    M --> O[HTTP /api/clusters]

docs.title: Package structure
docs.text:
cmd/
  clusterscope/
    main.go            # CLI entrypoint, flag parsing, mode dispatch

internal/
  graph/
    graph.go           # Shared data model: Node, Edge, Graph, ClusterProfile
  live/
    live.go            # GitOps status enrichment (Flux + ArgoCD)
    clients.go         # per-cluster kubeconfigs + reachability
    endpoints.go       # Gateway/HTTPRoute inventory
    workloads.go       # actual workload health per node + drift
  render/
    render.go          # HTML generation (WriteHTML, WriteIndex)
    template.html      # D3.js cluster profile template
    index.html         # Multi-cluster dashboard template
    shell.html         # HTMX serve-mode shell
  repos/
    repos.go           # repos.yaml schema for git-sync mode
  scan/
    scan.go            # Cluster directory discovery (flat / nested, lab from path) + tech detection
  serve/
    serve.go           # HTTP server, file watcher, cluster cache
    endpoints.go       # endpoint inventory API, probes, http_sd targets
    lab.go             # lab view: findings, summary, /api/lab

pkg/
  flux/
    parser.go          # Flux YAML parser (GitRepository, Kustomization, FluxInstance)
  argocd/
    parser.go          # ArgoCD parser (Application, ApplicationSet, AppProject)

kcl/                   # KCL deployment module (Kubernetes manifests)
dagger/                # Dagger CI module (lint, build, image, scan)

docs.title: Static mode
docs.text:
-dir <cluster>  →  ParseDir()  →  graph.ClusterProfile  →  WriteHTML()  →  .html file
-root <dir>     →  scan.Root() →  []ClusterProfile       →  WriteHTML() × N + WriteIndex()

docs.title: Serve mode
docs.text:
-serve :8080  →  serve.Start()
                 ├─ scanAll()  (on startup)
                 ├─ watch()    (fsnotify goroutine)
                 ├─ enrichAll() (if -live, periodic goroutine)
                 └─ HTTP handlers: /, /api/clusters, /clusters/<name>

docs.title: Live enrichment
docs.text:
live.Clients.Enrich(profile, cluster)
  ├─ resolve kubeconfig: -kubeconfig-map → -kubeconfig-dir/<cluster> → default (self only)
  ├─ GET /version                                     →  reachable | unreachable | unconfigured
  ├─ Flux:   list kustomizations + gitrepositories    →  status from Ready conditions
  ├─ ArgoCD: list applications                        →  status from health + sync
  └─ Gateway API: list gateways + httproutes          →  endpoint inventory (+ probe.ProbeAll with -probe)

docs.title: Technology detection
docs.text:
internal/scan.DetectTech(dir) reads YAML files in a directory and returns:

  • "argocd" if any file contains argoproj.io or kind: Application
  • "flux" otherwise

docs.title: repos.yaml (git-sync mode)
docs.text:
When deploying clusterscope in Kubernetes with a git-sync sidecar, a repos.yaml file configures which Git repositories are synced to the -root directory.

Pass the file path via -repos-config:

clusterscope -serve :8080 -root /data -repos-config /etc/git-sync/repos.yaml

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
repos:
  - name: prod-clusters
    url: https://github.com/my-org/gitops-clusters.git
    branch: main
    path: clusters/prod
    auth:
      secretRef: gitops-repo-secret

  - name: staging-clusters
    url: https://github.com/my-org/gitops-clusters.git
    branch: staging
    path: clusters/staging

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Required Description name ✓ Unique identifier for the repository url ✓ Git repository URL branch ✓ Branch to sync path — Subdirectory within the repo to use as cluster root auth.secretRef — Name of the Kubernetes Secret containing credentials

Note

The repos-config flag only informs clusterscope of which repos are configured. The actual git-sync is performed by the git-sync sidecar container — clusterscope only reads the synced files from disk.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/stuttgart-things/clusterscope.git
cd clusterscope
go build ./...
go test ./...

Requires Go 1.22+ and Task.

docs.title: Available tasks
docs.text:
task --list

Key tasks:

Task Description task lint Run golangci-lint via Dagger task test Run Go unit tests with race detector via Dagger (same as CI) task build-test-binary Build binary + smoke test (--help) via Dagger task build-output-binary Build binary to /tmp/go/build/ task build-scan-image-ko Build + push + scan container image task ui-serve ROOT=./clusters Run serve mode locally task ui-serve-live ROOT=./clusters Run serve mode with live enrichment task ui-static ROOT=./clusters Generate static HTML dashboard task render-manifests Render KCL Kubernetes manifests

docs.title: Running tests locally
docs.text: go test ./...

docs.title: Linting
docs.text:
task lint
# or directly:
dagger call -m ./dagger lint --src .

docs.title: Adding a new parser
docs.text:
1. Create pkg/<technology>/parser.go
  2. Implement ParseDir(dir string) (*graph.ClusterProfile, error)
  3. Populate graph.Node with Type, Layer, Sub, Source, Path, etc.
  4. Add technology detection in internal/scan/scan.go → DetectTech()
  5. Wire up in cmd/clusterscope/main.go and internal/serve/serve.go

docs.title: PR workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a feature branch: git checkout -b feature/my-feature
  2. Implement + test
  3. go build ./... && task lint
  4. Push and open a PR targeting main
  5. CI runs lint + build automatically

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Standard Go formatting (gofmt)
  • golangci-lint with project config
  • No panics in library code — return errors
  • Security: no credentials in HTML output, validate external inputs at boundaries

docs.title: Endpoint Inventory
docs.text:
With -live, clusterscope collects the Gateway API objects of every reachable cluster and answers "which URLs exist in this lab, where do they go, and do they work?" — across all clusters under -root.

HTTPRoutes are read live from the clusters, not from Git: many routes are generated (Helm chart values, KCL modules, Flux postBuild substitution) and only exist after rendering.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# inventory only (Gateway / HTTPRoute status)
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters/labul/vsphere -live -kubeconfig-dir /kubeconfigs

# plus a one-shot reachability probe of every route URL on each refresh
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters/labul/vsphere -live -kubeconfig-dir /kubeconfigs -probe
Flag Default Description -probe false Probe every HTTPRoute URL on each live refresh -probe-timeout 5s Per-URL probe timeout

Open Inventory → Endpoints in the dashboard sidebar (or /#endpoints, standalone at /endpoints). Filters (text, cluster, problems only) are kept in the URL, so a filtered view can be shared: /endpoints?cluster=platform-sthings&problems=1.

docs.title: What is collected
docs.text:
Per cluster, gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1:

Field Source hostnames, paths spec.hostnames, spec.rules[].matches[].path gateway spec.parentRefs (namespace/name[/section]) backends spec.rules[].backendRefs ([ns/]name:port) Accepted / ResolvedRefs status.parents[].conditions — True only if all parents report True owning app helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name → argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id → kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name → (Argo CD clusters) app.kubernetes.io/instance Gateways class, listeners, addresses, Accepted / Programmed

Clusters without Gateway API CRDs are shown as such, not as an error.

docs.title: URLs
docs.text: One URL per concrete hostname (wildcard hostnames are listed but not probed). The scheme comes from the parent Gateway's listener that matches the hostname (HTTPS → https, only HTTP → http, unknown → https). The root / is used when any rule matches /, otherwise the first path.

docs.title: Probe
docs.text:
With -probe, every URL is checked once per live refresh (concurrency 8):

Stage Failure means dns hostname does not resolve connect TCP connection failed tls handshake / certificate verification failed http status ≥ 500, or other HTTP error

A status below 500 counts as OK — 401, 403, 404 and redirects (not followed) mean routing, certificate and backend work and the application answered. For HTTPS the leaf certificate's expiry is reported; the UI flags certificates expiring in less than 14 days.

While a cluster's API server is unreachable, its last known routes are kept (marked stale) and still probed — an unreachable API server does not mean the applications are down.

The probe is a dashboard snapshot. Continuous probing and alerting belong in Prometheus + blackbox-exporter — see /api/targets.

docs.title: GET /api/endpoints[?cluster=<name>]
docs.text:
{
  "clusters": [{"name": "platform-sthings", "reachability": "reachable", "gatewayAPI": true, "collectedAt": "…"}],
  "gateways": [{"cluster": "platform-sthings", "namespace": "default", "name": "platform-sthings-gateway", "class": "cilium", "listeners": […], "programmed": "True"}],
  "routes": [{
    "cluster": "platform-sthings", "namespace": "argocd", "name": "argocd-server",
    "hostnames": ["argocd.platform.example.com"], "urls": ["https://argocd.platform.example.com"],
    "parents": [{"gateway": "default/platform-sthings-gateway", "accepted": "True", "resolvedRefs": "True"}],
    "backends": ["argocd-server:443"], "app": "argo-cd-httproute",
    "accepted": "True", "resolvedRefs": "True",
    "probes": [{"url": "https://argocd.platform.example.com", "ok": true, "statusCode": 200, "latencyMs": 38, "certExpiry": "…"}]
  }],
  "probing": true
}

docs.title: GET /api/targets[?cluster=<name>]
docs.text:
Prometheus http_sd format, one target group per route URL:

[{"targets": ["https://argocd.platform.example.com"], "labels": {"cluster": "platform-sthings", "namespace": "argocd", "route": "argocd-server", "app": "argo-cd-httproute"}}]

blackbox-exporter scrape config:

- job_name: blackbox-httproutes
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module: [http_2xx]
  http_sd_configs:
    - url: http://clusterscope.clusterscope.svc:8080/api/targets
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: __param_target
    - source_labels: [__param_target]
      target_label: instance
    - target_label: __address__
      replacement: blackbox-exporter.monitoring.svc:9115

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metric Labels Description clusterscope_httproute_accepted cluster, namespace, route 1 if all parent Gateways accepted the route, else 0. Removed while the cluster is unreachable.

docs.title: RBAC
docs.text: Read access on gateway.networking.k8s.io gateways and httproutes in every cluster (included in the KCL ClusterRole).

curl -L https://github.com/stuttgart-things/clusterscope/releases/latest/download/clusterscope-linux-amd64 \

docs.text:

Requires Go 1.22+.

docs.title: KCL Deployment
docs.text: clusterscope ships with a KCL deployment module (kcl/) that generates all Kubernetes manifests including an optional git-sync sidecar and HTTPRoute.

docs.title: Generated resources
docs.text: Resource Kind clusterscope Namespace clusterscope ServiceAccount clusterscope ClusterRole clusterscope ClusterRoleBinding clusterscope Service clusterscope Deployment clusterscope HTTPRoute (optional, when httpRouteEnabled: true)

docs.title: Deploy via task
docs.text:
# Deploy (uses KUBECONFIG env)
task deploy

# Deploy with custom kubeconfig
KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task deploy

# Deploy with custom profile
PROFILE=tests/my-profile.yaml KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task deploy

# Undeploy (removes all resources)
KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task undeploy

docs.title: Deploy manually
docs.text:
kcl run kcl/ -Y tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml | python3 -c "
import sys, yaml
data = yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin)
for m in data.get('manifests', []):
    print('---')
    print(yaml.dump(m, default_flow_style=False))
" | kubectl apply -f -

echo "done"! note KCL outputs a single YAML document with a manifests: list. kubectl apply requires separate YAML documents - the Python snippet splits them correctly.

docs.title: Deployment profile
docs.text:
Configuration is passed via a YAML file using KCL's kcl_options format:

# tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml
kcl_options:
  - key: config.image
    value: ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterscope:latest
  - key: config.namespace
    value: clusterscope
  - key: config.tech
    value: flux
  - key: config.dir
    value: /data/harvester/clusters
  - key: config.port
    value: "8080"
  - key: config.replicas
    value: "1"
  # git-sync sidecar
  - key: config.gitSyncEnabled
    value: "true"
  - key: config.gitSyncRepo
    value: https://github.com/org/repo
  - key: config.gitSyncBranch
    value: main
  - key: config.gitSyncPeriod
    value: 60s
  # HTTPRoute (Gateway API)
  - key: config.httpRouteEnabled
    value: "true"
  - key: config.gatewayName
    value: my-gateway
  - key: config.gatewayNamespace
    value: default
  - key: config.hostname
    value: clusterscope
  - key: config.domain
    value: example.com

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: Key Default Description config.name clusterscope Resource name config.namespace clusterscope Kubernetes namespace config.image ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterscope:latest Container image config.imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent Image pull policy config.replicas 1 Number of replicas config.port 8080 HTTP serve port config.dir /data Path inside container to scan for GitOps manifests config.tech flux GitOps technology: flux or argocd config.gitSyncEnabled false Enable git-sync sidecar config.gitSyncImage registry.k8s.io/git-sync/git-sync:v4.4.0 git-sync image config.gitSyncRepo "" Git repository URL to sync (single-repo mode) config.gitSyncBranch main Branch/ref to sync (single-repo mode) config.gitSyncPeriod 60s Sync interval (single-repo mode) config.gitSyncAuthSecretName "" K8s Secret name for private repo auth config.gitSyncAuthType https Auth type: https (token) or ssh config.gitSyncRepos [] List of GitSyncRepo objects for multi-repo mode config.httpRouteEnabled false Create HTTPRoute (Gateway API) config.gatewayName "" Gateway name to attach the HTTPRoute to config.gatewayNamespace default Namespace of the Gateway config.hostname "" Hostname prefix (e.g. clusterscope) config.domain "" Domain (e.g. example.com) - URL: hostname.domain

docs.title: git-sync sidecar
docs.text:
When gitSyncEnabled: true, a git-sync sidecar is added. Both containers share an emptyDir volume at /data:

pod
+-- container: clusterscope  (-root=/data/<repo>/clusters -tech=flux -serve=:8080)
|   +-- volumeMount: gitdata -> /data
+-- container: git-sync      (--repo=... --ref=main --root=/data --period=60s)
    +-- volumeMount: gitdata -> /data

git-sync creates: /data/<repo-name> -> .worktrees/<hash> (symlink). Set config.dir to the subfolder inside the repo that contains the cluster directories, e.g. /data/harvester/clusters.

docs.title: Private repository authentication
docs.text: For private repositories, set gitSyncAuthSecretName and gitSyncAuthType.

docs.title: HTTPS (token/password)
docs.text:
kubectl create secret generic git-sync-auth \
  --from-literal=username=token \
  --from-literal=password=<GITHUB_TOKEN> \
  -n clusterscope

- key: config.gitSyncAuthSecretName
  value: git-sync-auth
- key: config.gitSyncAuthType
  value: https

docs.title: SSH key
docs.text:
kubectl create secret generic git-sync-ssh \
  --from-file=ssh=/home/user/.ssh/id_rsa \
  -n clusterscope

- key: config.gitSyncAuthSecretName
  value: git-sync-ssh
- key: config.gitSyncAuthType
  value: ssh

docs.title: Multi-repo mode
docs.text:
To monitor multiple repositories simultaneously, use gitSyncRepos instead of gitSyncRepo. Each entry creates a dedicated git-sync-<subdir> sidecar that syncs into /data/<subdir>/:

- key: config.gitSyncRepos
  value:
    - repo: https://github.com/org/harvester
      branch: main
      subdir: harvester     # syncs into /data/harvester/
      period: 60s
    - repo: https://github.com/org/clusters
      branch: main
      subdir: st-clusters   # syncs into /data/st-clusters/
      period: 120s
      authSecretName: git-sync-auth   # optional: private repo
      authType: https

Set config.dir to /data — clusterscope scans all subdirectories automatically:

- key: config.dir
  value: /data

Resulting pod layout:

pod
+-- container: clusterscope         (-root=/data -tech=flux -serve=:8080)
+-- container: git-sync-harvester   (--root=/data/harvester)
+-- container: git-sync-st-clusters (--root=/data/st-clusters)

Note: gitSyncRepos takes priority over gitSyncRepo. Existing single-repo profiles continue to work unchanged.

docs.title: HTTPRoute
docs.text:
When httpRouteEnabled: true, a Gateway API HTTPRoute is generated pointing to the clusterscope Service:

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: clusterscope
  namespace: clusterscope
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: <gatewayName>
      namespace: <gatewayNamespace>
  hostnames:
    - "<hostname>.<domain>"
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: clusterscope
          port: 8080

kcl run kcl/ -Y tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml

docs.title: Alternative: Deploy via OCI Kustomize artifact
docs.text: Instead of rendering with KCL locally, you can deploy using the pre-built Kustomize OCI artifact published to ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterscope-kustomize.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • oras CLI for pulling OCI artifacts

docs.title: Overlay structure
docs.text:
tests/kustomize-overlay/
├── kustomization.yaml      # references ./base + patches
├── deployment-patch.yaml   # strategic merge patch (git-sync sidecar, args)
└── httproute.yaml          # HTTPRoute (cluster-specific)
    base/                   # populated by task deploy-kustomize (git-ignored)

docs.title: Deploy via task
docs.text:
# Deploy (pulls OCI base + applies overlay)
KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task deploy-kustomize

# Deploy with custom OCI tag
OCI_TAG=v0.6.0 KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task deploy-kustomize

# Undeploy
KUBECONFIG_PATH=~/.kube/my-cluster task undeploy-kustomize

docs.title: Deploy manually
docs.text:
# 1. Pull OCI base
mkdir -p tests/kustomize-overlay/base
oras pull ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterscope-kustomize:v0.6.0 \
  -o tests/kustomize-overlay/base

# 2. Apply overlay (base + deployment-patch + httproute)
kubectl apply -k tests/kustomize-overlay/

docs.title: Customize the overlay
docs.text:
deployment-patch.yaml — strategic merge patch to add git-sync sidecar and set -root:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: clusterscope
  namespace: clusterscope
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: clusterscope
          args:
            - '-root=/data/<repo>/clusters'   # path inside synced repo
            - '-tech=flux'
            - '-serve=:8080'
        - name: git-sync
          image: registry.k8s.io/git-sync/git-sync:v4.4.0
          args:
            - '--repo=https://github.com/org/repo'
            - '--ref=main'
            - '--root=/data'
            - '--period=60s'
            - '--depth=1'
          ...

httproute.yaml — HTTPRoute (adapt gateway name and hostname):

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: clusterscope
  namespace: clusterscope
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: my-gateway
      namespace: default
  hostnames:
    - clusterscope.example.com
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: clusterscope
          port: 8080

docs.title: Lab View
docs.text:
The lab view answers "what runs where in a lab?": Lab → Cluster → App → Endpoint, with the desired state (Git), the GitOps status and the actual state side by side. Every mismatch is listed as a finding.

Open it via Inventory → Lab overview in the dashboard sidebar (/#lab), or directly at /lab. Filters (text, lab, severity) are kept in the URL.

docs.title: Cluster discovery and labs
docs.text:
-root can point at a single cluster, at a directory of clusters, or at a whole repo tree:

-root contains Clusters subdirectories with YAML files each subdirectory (flat layout) YAML files itself -root is the only cluster neither searched recursively (up to 4 levels): a directory with YAML files is a cluster, one without is descended into

The lab is taken from the path: the segment after clusters/ when at least one more segment follows before the cluster directory.

clusters/labul/vsphere/platform-sthings   → lab labul
clusters/labda/vsphere/machinery          → lab labda
harvester/clusters/edge                   → -lab (or "default")

So -root ./clusters shows all labs of the repo at once, and -root ./clusters/labul/vsphere shows one lab. Use -lab <name> for clusters whose path does not name a lab, and for clusters that only have a kubeconfig.

Cluster names must be unique (they are also the kubeconfig names). A second directory with the same name is skipped and reported as duplicate name.

Directories with no GitOps object (no Flux Kustomization / source, no Argo CD Application), and with no reachable cluster behind them, are listed but not counted as clusters. These are typically Crossplane claims or clusterbook data next to the cluster directories.

The file watcher covers root, every cluster directory and the directories in between; any change triggers a debounced full rescan, and removed directories disappear from the dashboard and the metrics.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Source Provides cluster directories (Git) desired state: clusters, Kustomizations / Applications -kubeconfig-dir / -kubeconfig-map which clusters can be reached live mode GitOps status, workload health, endpoints

clusterbook (IPs/DNS) and machinery (ordered clusters) are planned as further sources.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Severity Kind Meaning error unreachable cluster directory in Git, API server unreachable error scan error cluster directory could not be parsed error GitOps failed Kustomization / Application / FluxInstance not ready error drift GitOps ready, but workloads degraded/down or a HelmRelease not ready error workloads down all workloads down (GitOps not failed) error endpoint down an HTTPRoute URL failed the probe (-probe) warning no kubeconfig cluster directory in Git, but no kubeconfig: actual state unknown warning not in Git (cluster) kubeconfig present, but no cluster directory in any scanned repo warning not deployed Kustomization / Application in Git, but not in the cluster warning workloads degraded some replicas missing or pod issues (GitOps not failed) warning route HTTPRoute not Accepted / ResolvedRefs warning workloads unreadable workloads/pods could not be listed (RBAC) warning duplicate name second directory with an existing cluster name info not in Git (object) Kustomization / Application in the cluster without any GitOps manager: applied by hand

Kustomizations / Applications in the cluster that are not in the cluster directory but were created by another GitOps object (labels kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name, helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name, fluxcd.controlplane.io/name, app.kubernetes.io/instance, annotation argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id, or an owner reference) are nested: they are in Git elsewhere. They are counted per cluster (+N nested), not reported.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
GET /api/lab

  "generatedAt": "2026-10-14T17:57:45Z",

GET /api/clusters carries the lab of every cluster; the sidebar groups clusters by lab when there is more than one.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metric Labels Value clusterscope_lab_findings lab, severity, kind number of findings clusterscope_cluster_info cluster, lab, tech, managed always 1; managed="false" for kubeconfig-only clusters

clusterscope_cluster_info lets you group the other per-cluster metrics by lab:

sum by (lab) (clusterscope_app_gitops_drift * on(cluster) group_left(lab) clusterscope_cluster_info)

docs.title: Live Mode
docs.text: Live mode enriches the static YAML-parsed graph with real-time reconciliation status fetched from the Kubernetes API (client-go, no kubectl required).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Inside Kubernetes: the pod's ServiceAccount, or
  • a kubeconfig (-kubeconfig, KUBECONFIG env, ~/.kube/config), or
  • one kubeconfig per cluster (-kubeconfig-dir / -kubeconfig-map, see below)
  • Cluster API access (read-only on the relevant CRDs)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Serve with live enrichment
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters -live -kubeconfig ~/.kube/prod

# Single-cluster static with live
clusterscope -dir ./clusters/prod -tech flux -live -kubeconfig ~/.kube/prod -out live.html

# Custom refresh interval (default: 30s)
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters -live -refresh 60

# Multi-cluster: one kubeconfig per cluster
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters/labul/vsphere -live \
  -kubeconfig-dir /kubeconfigs -self-cluster platform-sthings

docs.title: Multi-cluster live mode
docs.text:
With only -kubeconfig (or in-cluster), every cluster under -root is enriched from that one cluster. This is fine for a single cluster, but in a multi-cluster dashboard all other clusters would show the status of the wrong cluster.

Per-cluster kubeconfigs fix this:

Flag Description -kubeconfig-dir Directory with one kubeconfig file per cluster, named after the cluster directory (e.g. /kubeconfigs/infra-sthings). Fits a mounted Secret with one key per cluster. -kubeconfig-map YAML file for names that do not match (see below). Relative paths are resolved against -kubeconfig-dir. -self-cluster The cluster clusterscope runs in. Only this cluster falls back to -kubeconfig / in-cluster. 
# -kubeconfig-map
clusters:
  platform-sthings: labul-platform.yaml
  homerun2-test1: /kubeconfigs/labul/homerun2-test1

Resolution per cluster, as soon as -kubeconfig-dir or -kubeconfig-map is set:

  1. -kubeconfig-map entry
  2. -kubeconfig-dir/<cluster>
  3. -kubeconfig / in-cluster — only for -self-cluster
  4. otherwise unconfigured (no live status, nodes unknown)

Clients are cached per kubeconfig file and rebuilt when the file changes (Secret rotation). Clusters are refreshed in parallel, so one unreachable API server does not delay the others.

docs.title: Cluster reachability
docs.text:
Before enrichment, clusterscope calls GET /version on the cluster's API server.

Reachability Meaning reachable API server answered and accepted the credentials unreachable Connection failed, timed out (10s), or credentials were rejected (401/403) unconfigured No kubeconfig resolved for this cluster

For unreachable and unconfigured clusters all nodes are reset to unknown, so a cluster that goes down does not keep showing its last known status.

Reachability is exposed in:

  • GET /api/clusters — reachability and liveError per cluster
  • the dashboard sidebar — red ring + unreachable / no kubeconfig
  • /metrics — clusterscope_cluster_reachable{cluster="…"} (1 / 0, absent when unconfigured)

docs.title: Status values
docs.text: Status Color Meaning ready 🟢 Green Resource reconciled successfully failed 🔴 Red Reconciliation failed progressing 🟠 Orange Reconciliation in progress unknown Grey Cluster unreachable / unconfigured, or no status available

docs.title: Workload health
docs.text:
The GitOps status only reflects the last reconcile: Flux evaluates health checks during a reconcile, so with interval: 1h a Ready=True can be an hour old while the pods behind it crash-loop. clusterscope therefore evaluates the actual workloads of every node at each refresh.

Which workloads belong to a node

Node Objects Flux Kustomization .status.inventory — Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets listed directly, plus all workloads labelled helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name / -namespace for every HelmRelease in the inventory sync-root (flux-operator) the FluxInstance inventory (the Flux controllers) Argo CD Application .status.resources

Nested Kustomizations are not followed: a Kustomization that only creates other Kustomizations reports n/a, its children report their own workloads.

Per workload: available / desired replicas (Deployment availableReplicas, StatefulSet availableReplicas/readyReplicas, DaemonSet numberAvailable vs. desiredNumberScheduled) and the pods matched by its selector:

  • containers waiting in CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull, CreateContainerConfigError, …
  • containers that are not ready and have restarted (restarting (last exit: Error, code 1)) — catches a crash loop in the seconds between two back-offs
  • pods Pending for more than 2 minutes
  • container restarts since the previous refresh
Workload status Meaning healthy all workloads have all desired replicas available, no pod issues (scaled to 0 counts as healthy) degraded some replicas missing, or pod issues down no workload has a single available replica n/a the node manages no Deployments, StatefulSets or DaemonSets

Drift is set when the GitOps controller reports the node ready while its workloads are degraded/down or one of its HelmReleases is not ready — exactly the state Flux hides until the next reconcile.

Shown in:

  • the dependency graph — ready/total badge on each node, dashed border on drift
  • the detail panel — every workload with replicas, pod issues and restarts, every HelmRelease with its Ready condition, and the age of the last Ready transition next to the interval
  • the dashboard sidebar — n degraded · n down · n drift per cluster
  • GET /api/clusters — workloadSummary, drift, workloadError; the node JSON carries workloads
  • /metrics:
Metric Labels Value clusterscope_app_workload_status cluster, app, status 1 for the current status (healthy, degraded, down, n/a), 0 for the others clusterscope_app_gitops_drift cluster, app 1 on drift, else 0

Alert on these in Prometheus instead of watching the UI, e.g.:

- alert: GitOpsDrift
  expr: clusterscope_app_gitops_drift == 1
  for: 15m
  annotations:
    summary: "{{ $labels.app }} on {{ $labels.cluster }} is GitOps-ready but its workloads are not"

If workloads or pods cannot be listed (missing RBAC), the cluster shows workloads unreadable and workloadError — GitOps status is still reported.

docs.title: UI changes in live mode
docs.text:
• Node border color reflects live status (instead of type color)
  • Clicking a node shows Status, Message, the last transition and the workload health in the detail panel
  • A 🟢 Live · <timestamp> badge appears in the cluster profile header

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• No credentials are written to HTML output
  • KUBECONFIG follows standard kubectl conventions
  • -kubeconfig and -kubeconfig-dir are validated (must exist) before the server starts
  • Live errors degrade to status: "unknown" — the server never crashes on live failures
  • Only read access is needed on workload clusters (get/list on the Flux / Argo CD CRDs, apps workloads and pods for workload health, and gateway.networking.k8s.io for the endpoint inventory)

docs.title: PDF Export
docs.text: Every cluster profile HTML page includes a 🖨 Print / Save as PDF button in the header.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Open a cluster profile in your browser (served or static HTML)
  2. Click 🖨 Print / Save as PDF in the top-right header
  3. In the browser print dialog, select Save as PDF → A4

Or use the keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+P / Cmd+P

docs.title: Print layout
docs.text:
The @media print CSS automatically:

  • Hides interactive elements: filter bar, graph SVG, detail panel, toggle buttons, search box
  • Shows print-only summary tables:
  • Kustomizations (Name, Path, Version, Domain, DependsOn)
  • Git Sources (Name, URL, Branch, Interval)
  • ArgoCD Applications (Name, Project, Repo, Path, Revision, Namespace)
  • Applies a light-on-white color scheme (GitHub light style)
  • Sets A4 page size with 1.5cm margins
  • Adds page breaks between sections

docs.title: No extra dependencies
docs.text: PDF export is implemented purely via browser CSS — no Chromium, no Go PDF library, no additional binaries required.

docs.title: PR Preview
docs.text: clusterscope can show an interactive visual diff of what a pull request would change in the GitOps cluster graph — added, removed, and modified resources with field-level change details.

docs.title: Local testing with the dashboard
docs.text:
The fastest way to try PR preview locally:

# Point clusterscope at your clusters directory
# Use the parent of the cluster dirs so they appear in the sidebar
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters/labul/vsphere

# Open http://localhost:8080

In the sidebar, fill in the PR Preview form:

  • Repository URL: https://github.com/stuttgart-things/stuttgart-things
  • PR #: 1919
  • Cluster: movie-scripts

Click Preview Diff. Clusterscope will:

  1. Shallow-clone the repo at refs/pull/1919/head
  2. Also clone the base branch (main) for comparison
  3. Recursively discover cluster directories in both clones
  4. Diff the two graphs and render the result

The diff view shows:

  • Color-coded nodes: green (added), red (removed), orange (modified), dimmed (unchanged)
  • Before / After / Diff view toggle
  • Filter toggles for each diff kind
  • Click any node for field-level change details
  • Changes panel listing all modifications

Results are cached for 5 minutes — subsequent requests for the same repo+ref are instant.

docs.title: CLI diff mode
docs.text:
Compare two local directories directly:

# Markdown output (default) — for PR comments
clusterscope -diff \
  -base-dir ./clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
  -head-dir ./pr-branch/clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts

# JSON output — for CI pipelines
clusterscope -diff \
  -base-dir ./clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
  -head-dir ./pr-branch/clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
  -format json

# HTML output — interactive diff visualization
clusterscope -diff \
  -base-dir ./clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
  -head-dir ./pr-branch/clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
  -format html -out diff.html

docs.title: Example markdown output
docs.text:
## Clusterscope Diff: movie-scripts

**-4** removed | 16 unchanged

### Removed
- ~~`claim-machinery-api`~~ (apps)
- ~~`machinery`~~ (apps)
- ~~`tekton`~~ (apps)
- ~~`tekton-dashboard-httproute`~~ (apps)

### Edge Changes
- - ~~`flux-apps` → `claim-machinery-api`~~ (watches)
- - ~~`flux-apps` → `machinery`~~ (watches)
- - ~~`flux-apps` → `tekton-dashboard-httproute`~~ (watches)
- - ~~`flux-apps` → `tekton`~~ (watches)
- - ~~`tekton` → `tekton-dashboard-httproute`~~ (dependsOn)

docs.title: GitHub Actions integration
docs.text:
Post the diff as a PR comment automatically:

- name: Checkout base
  uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
    path: base

- name: Checkout head
  uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    path: head

- name: GitOps Preview
  run: |
    clusterscope -diff \
      -base-dir base/clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
      -head-dir head/clusters/labul/vsphere/movie-scripts \
      -format markdown > preview.md

- name: Comment on PR
  run: gh pr comment ${{ github.event.number }} --body-file preview.md
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

docs.title: On-demand preview API
docs.text:
The dashboard's PR preview form uses these endpoints:

Endpoint Description GET /preview/<cluster>?repo=<url>&pr=<N> HTML diff visualization GET /api/preview/<cluster>?repo=<url>&pr=<N> JSON diff data GET /preview/<cluster>?repo=<url>&ref=<ref> Preview any git ref (branch, tag) GET /api/preview/<cluster>?repo=<url>&ref=<ref>&base=<branch> Override base branch (default: main)

docs.title: Query parameters
docs.text: Param Description repo Git repository URL (required for on-demand mode) pr Pull request number — constructs refs/pull/N/head ref Git ref to preview (alternative to pr) base Base branch for comparison (default: main)

docs.title: Private repositories
docs.text:
On-demand preview inherits the git auth from the environment. If your local git can fetch the repo, PR preview will work:

# These all work if configured:
# - SSH keys (~/.ssh/*)
# - Git credential helpers (gh auth, git-credential-manager)
# - GH_TOKEN environment variable
# - .netrc

In Kubernetes, mount a git credential secret or set GH_TOKEN as a pod env var.

docs.title: Sidecar-based preview
docs.text:
For persistent preview of a specific PR (e.g., in a staging environment), use the git-sync sidecar approach instead of on-demand cloning:

clusterscope -serve :8080 -root /data/base -preview-root /data/head

See KCL Deployment for the previewEnabled configuration that deploys a second git-sync sidecar targeting a PR ref.

docs.title: Diff flags reference
docs.text: Flag Default Description -diff false Enable diff mode -base-dir — Base cluster directory (required with -diff) -head-dir — Head cluster directory (required with -diff) -format markdown Output format: markdown, json, html -out stdout Output file path -tech flux Technology: flux or argocd

docs.title: Serve Mode
docs.text: clusterscope can run as a persistent HTTP dashboard server that watches your cluster directories for changes and serves interactive HTML profiles.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
clusterscope -serve :8080 -root ./clusters

Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. On startup, the cluster directories below -root are discovered (flat or nested clusters/<lab>/…/<cluster>, see Lab View) and parsed
  2. Technology is auto-detected per cluster (Flux vs ArgoCD)
  3. A file watcher monitors -root, the cluster directories and the directories in between
  4. Changes are debounced (500ms) and trigger a re-scan; removed directories disappear
  5. The /api/clusters endpoint returns a JSON summary of all clusters
  6. /clusters/<name> returns the HTML profile for a specific cluster

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Path Description / HTMX shell with cluster selector and PR preview form /api/clusters JSON list of cluster summaries /clusters/<name> HTML profile for cluster <name> /lab Lab view: all clusters per lab, desired vs. actual, findings /api/lab Lab view as JSON /endpoints Endpoint inventory (live mode) /api/endpoints Endpoint inventory as JSON /api/targets Route URLs in Prometheus http_sd format /preview/<name>?repo=<url>&pr=<N> On-demand PR diff visualization /api/preview/<name>?repo=<url>&pr=<N> On-demand PR diff as JSON /healthz Liveness probe /readyz Readiness probe /metrics Prometheus metrics /pdf/<name> PDF export via headless Chromium

docs.title: Taskfile
docs.text:
task ui-serve ROOT=./clusters PORT=8080
task ui-serve-live ROOT=./clusters KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/prod

docs.title: PR preview in the dashboard
docs.text: The sidebar includes a PR Preview form. Enter a repository URL, PR number, and cluster name to see an interactive diff visualization. See PR Preview for details.

docs.title: Kubernetes deployment
docs.text: See KCL Deployment for running clusterscope in a cluster with a git-sync sidecar that keeps -root synchronized from a Git repository.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: clusterscope [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Default Description -dir . Path to the cluster directory to visualize -tech flux Technology to parse: flux or argocd -out stdout Output file path (.html) -root . Root directory: one cluster, a directory of clusters, or a repo tree (see Lab View) -lab default Lab name for clusters whose path does not contain clusters/<lab>/… -serve — Start HTTP dashboard server (e.g. :8080) -live false Enrich graph with real-time status from the Kubernetes API -kubeconfig — Path to default kubeconfig file -kubeconfig-dir — Directory with one kubeconfig per cluster (see Live Mode) -kubeconfig-map — YAML mapping cluster name → kubeconfig path -self-cluster — Cluster clusterscope runs in (uses -kubeconfig / in-cluster) -probe false Probe every HTTPRoute URL on each live refresh (see Endpoint Inventory) -probe-timeout 5s Per-URL probe timeout -refresh 30 Live status refresh interval in seconds -repos-config — Path to repos.yaml (git-sync Kubernetes mode) -diff false Compare two cluster directories and output a diff -base-dir — Base cluster directory (used with -diff) -head-dir — Head cluster directory (used with -diff) -format markdown Diff output format: markdown | json | html -preview-root — PR head ref cluster files (used with -serve)

clusterscope -dir ./clusters/prod
clusterscope -dir ./clusters/prod -out profile.html
